description: This round's FIND-1004 fix correctly adds `balanceUsd` to REQ-117 step 6's getCitizen return-shape enumeration, but does NOT act on FIND-1004's own explicit recommendation to 'remove the vague trailing `...`' -- the enumeration (behavioral-spec.md line 2614) still reads `{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, balanceUsd, ...}`. This review empirically confirmed, via REAL execution against the unmodified `lending-orchestrator.mjs`/`lending-gate.mjs`, that this residual trailing-`...` ambiguity is NOT cosmetic: it is the ONLY textual signal that could cover two OTHER fields the SAME re-check code path also requires -- `fuel` and `humanDependencies` -- and a getCitizen closure built from a literal, narrow reading of the explicitly-named field list (exactly the reading that produced FIND-1004's own balanceUsd omission) reproduces the IDENTICAL silent-refusal defect class, just via a different missing field and a different refusal reason. `runLockedIssuance`'s step-6 fresh recheck calls `isBorrowerEligible({borrowerAgent: freshBorrower, ...})` (lending-orchestrator.mjs:194-200), which calls `isSelfFunded(borrowerAgent)` (lending-gate.mjs:108) directly on whatever `getCitizen` returned for the borrower -- and `isSelfFunded` (`_shared/lib/is-self-funded.mjs:68-70`) fail-closed-denies (`hasOwnWallet(agent) && fuelIsOwnFunded(agent) && hasNoHumanDependency(agent)`) unless the object carries a recognized `agent.fuel.provider` AND an `agent.humanDependencies` array with `.length===0` -- neither of which appears anywhere in step 6's own enumerated field list. This is the SAME mechanism, SAME severity class, and SAME silent (non-crashing, exit-0, indistinguishable-from-a-healthy-no-op) failure mode FIND-1004 just fixed for `balanceUsd` -- discovered because the fix pattern this feature has followed for 2 consecutive rounds (FIND-1004 this round, the crash fix FIND-1003 the round before) is REACTIVE: patch the ONE field the LAST finding named, without addressing why a hand-curated field-enumeration approach keeps omitting load-bearing fields one at a time. Two readings of the text exist: (a) 'returns that SAME citizen record shape steps 1-5 already consume' (the prose immediately preceding the bracketed shape) could mean the closure passes through the REAL registry record object wholesale (which would already include `fuel`/`humanDependencies`, since step 4's own `isSelfFunded(citizen)` filter already requires them on the SAME registry read) -- under this reading there is no bug; (b) the bracketed `{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, balanceUsd, ...}` is read as the authoritative field list to hand-construct -- under this reading (the SAME reading that produced FIND-1004), the object is missing `fuel`/`humanDependencies` and the borrower is silently, permanently refused as `not_self_funded` regardless of its real qualification. Because reading (b) is not merely hypothetical -- it is the EXACT reading responsible for FIND-1004 one round ago -- and because the trailing `...` FIND-1004 asked to have removed is still present, this ambiguity remains live and, per this review's own empirical test, still exploitable.

evidence.snippet: returns that SAME citizen record shape steps 1-5 already consume, PLUS a fresh `balanceUsd` field ... `{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, balanceUsd, ...}` -- `balanceUsd` fetched via the SAME `_shared/lib/usdc.mjs::usdcBalance(...)` primitive step 4 already uses
const eligibility = isBorrowerEligible({ borrowerAgent: freshBorrower, loanRows, borrowerId, borrowerBalanceUsd: freshBorrower.balanceUsd, lenderId });

function hasOwnWallet(agent) {...Boolean(wallet.evm) || Boolean(wallet.solana)} ... function fuelIsOwnFunded(agent) {...OWN_FUNDED_FUEL_PROVIDERS.has(provider)} ... function hasNoHumanDependency(agent) {...deps.length === 0} ... export function isSelfFunded(agent) { return hasOwnWallet(agent) && fuelIsOwnFunded(agent) && hasNoHumanDependency(agent); }

evidence.location: fresh execution this review, `node` against the real, unmodified lending-orchestrator.mjs/lending-gate.mjs/is-self-funded.mjs, deps.getCitizen returning EXACTLY the literal enumerated shape `{id, wallet:{evm:true}, walletAddress:{evm}, coLocatedWithCoordinator:true, balanceUsd}` -- no `fuel`, no `humanDependencies` -- for a fixture representing PROP-117c's own fixture-3 scenario (one broke, one surplus, both otherwise fully qualifying, self-funded per the ORIGINAL registry record used at step 4's own filter)
evidence.description: `await executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId:'lenderA', borrowerId:'borrowerB', nowMs}, {getCitizen, gojoLogRows:[], ledgerFile, lockStatePath, disburse: stub})` (correct 2-argument call, `balanceUsd` present per this round's own fix) returned `{"status":"refused","reason":"not_self_funded"}` -- a silent, permanent, exit-0 refusal, for the exact fixture-3 scenario PROP-117c is named to prove reaches `active`. A control run with the SAME shape PLUS `fuel:{provider:"x402"}, humanDependencies:[]` reached `{"status":"active","loanId":"loan_lenderA_1"}`, confirming `fuel`/`humanDependencies` (not `balanceUsd` this time) are the missing ingredient under this literal reading.

recommendation: Replace the field-enumeration approach entirely rather than patching another named field: state that `deps.getCitizen`'s closure SHALL return the REAL registry record object for that id (the SAME object step 1's `ensureCitizensRegistry` read already produces and step 4 already runs `isSelfFunded`/`coLocatedWithCoordinator`/`wallet.evm` checks against), with a fresh `balanceUsd` field MERGED on via object spread (`{...registryCitizen, balanceUsd}`) -- NEVER a hand-typed object literal naming a subset of fields. Delete the bracketed `{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, balanceUsd, ...}` illustrative shape entirely (per FIND-1004's own already-stated, not-yet-acted-on instruction to remove the trailing `...`) since ANY enumerated-subset shape is structurally prone to omitting whatever field the NEXT downstream consumer happens to need (this round: `fuel`/`humanDependencies` for `isSelfFunded`; a future round could just as easily be some other field some other consumer needs) -- this is the same defect class recurring for a third time (FIND-1003: missing 2nd arg entirely; FIND-1004: missing `balanceUsd`; this finding: missing `fuel`/`humanDependencies`), and only a 'full record, never a subset' instruction closes the whole class at once rather than one field at a time.
